title: Train a digit reader from scratch
brief: Build a regularised, gradient-checked, early-stopped network in numpy that reads noisy 10 by 10 digits and clearly beats a linear baseline.
hints: He initialisation draws W with scale sqrt(2 / n_in), where n_in is the number of rows of W, because this project stores W as (n_in, n_out) and computes h @ W.
Keep the dropout mask in the cache. The backward pass multiplies by the same mask, and a mask redrawn there gives a gradient that no finite difference matches.
In backward, the order going back through a hidden layer is: multiply by W.T, then by the dropout mask, then by (z > 0).
If gradient_check reports an error above 1e-4, test one layer at a time: set the other layers' gradients aside and compare only W of the last layer first.
Return a copy of the parameters from the best validation epoch, not the parameters from the last epoch.
